text:
alex: FYI customer reported weird TS resolution when importing the SDK from Next middleware: editor shows types but build fails with "Cannot find module '@redwood/inference/edge' or its corresponding type declarations."

maya: interesting. are they using `moduleResolution: node` or `bundler`? Next SWC sometimes rewrites imports and TS path resolution can differ at build time.

sam: quick summary of root cause we found: we published conditional exports for ESM/CJS but didn't include `types` pointers in the exports map. V8/bundlers pick `./edge` fine, but tsc/VSCode follow `types` field and fallback to the top-level `types` which points at cjs dts. results: runtime ESM ok, compile-time fails.

ben: repro steps I used locally: 1) scaffold a Next app with `edge` middleware 2) `npm i @redwood/inference@local` 3) add `import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` in middleware.ts 4) `next dev` fails with the error above.

lina: plan: add "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts" and `exports: { "./edge": { "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs", "types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts" }, ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs", "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts" } }`. that should satisfy TS and bundlers.

ryan: caution: typesVersions is useful for older TS, but can be confusing. I lean to explicit `exports`->`types` per subpath. also add `packageExportsTest` script to CI that runs `node -p "require.resolve('@redwood/inference/edge')"` and `ts-node -e "import('@redwood/inference/edge')"` or similar.

alex: another gotcha: Next's SWC sometimes marks files with "edge" as browser platform and strips `process.env` which our types reference in JSDoc generics — that makes editors complain. we should keep the edge entry purely runtime and move config typing to the shared types file.

maya: also saw that some folks `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` expecting a default export. we currently export named `Redwood`. If we add `export default Redwood` in the ESM edge entry it'll reduce confusion for folks doing quick JS imports in middleware. but TS users will still import named.

sam: small tradeoff but pragmatic. add a tiny edge entry file that re-exports only the minimal runtime surface and `export default` for JS ergonomics. something like:
```js
// dist/edge/index.mjs
import { Redwood } from '../esm/index.mjs';
export { Redwood };
export default Redwood;
```

ben: for CI, add a job that does: `pnpm build:dist && node ./test-scripts/check-exports.js` where the script verifies `require.resolve`, `import()` and `tsc --noEmit` against a fixture Next project. catches both runtime and type regressions.

lina: docs update: show three patterns for middleware usage: `await import('@redwood/inference/edge')` (recommended), `import() default` for plain JS, and `import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` with a note about SWC/TS resolution. include snippet for esbuild bundling targets.

ryan: one more subtle issue: some users bundle with older esbuild targets and end up with `globalThis.fetch` polyfilled incorrectly. let's document required targets: es2020+ and `platform: browser` for edge bundles. mention not to include node polyfills.

deploy-bot: created PR #1310: add exports.types and edge entry + CI job. preview deploy at branch `sdk/edge-exports` :white_check_mark:

alex: action items: maya add default export shim, ben add CI export checks, sam update package.json + build scripts, lina update docs + examples. I'll follow up on the PR review. thanks team! :rocket:
